## Specifications

- **2WD C200K standard ratio**: 2.93 [t353] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **4WD M226 (Auto) ratio**: 3.13 [t353] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **C200K bolt count**: 8 [t353] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **M226 bolt count**: 12 [t353] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Manual X/S/SE M226 ratio**: 3.54 [t353] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Pro-4X Auto M226 ratio**: 3.36 [t353] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Pro-4X Manual M226 ratio**: 3.69 [t353] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Understand that 2WD models typically come with a C200K and 2.93 gearing. [t353]
- [Partial] Recognize that 4WD M226 units are identical to their 2WD counterparts, making them easier to source. [t353]
- Use a 3.13 gear for better low-end power without changing tire size. [t353]
- Consider an Auto Pro-4X/M226 with 3.36 gears if planning to upgrade tires to 285s. [t353]
- [Partial] Stock M226 ratios often sit around 3.54 to 3.73. [t353]
- Higher ratios like 4.10 or 4.56 may require matching front diffs and potentially unequal length shafts. [t353]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Assuming 'Off Road' trim is exclusive to the Pro-4X generation (2011+) without verifying door badges. [t353]
- [Partial] Confusing automatic transmission gear ratios with manual ones when sourcing parts. [t353]
